name: sim_weyl_pairwise_a2_bc2_coupling
scope_note: Pairwise coupling probe: W(A2) <-> W(B2/C2). Step 2 of coupling program. W(A2)=S3 (order 6) and W(B2)=Dih4 (order 8) are non-isomorphic; they share W(A1)=Z2 subgroup but have distinct Coxeter orders (3 vs 4). Cross-group reflections do not commute; A2 reflections escape B2 root set. z3 UNSAT: 6==8 arithmetic impossibility.

pytorch.reason: Represent both A2 (6 roots) and B2 (8 roots) as 2D float64 tensors; apply cross-group reflections; compute ||s_A2(s_B2(v)) - s_B2(s_A2(v))|| as the non-commutativity measure; check A2 reflections map B2 roots outside B2

z3.reason: UNSAT: |W(A2)| = |W(B2)| — encode 6 == 8 as Z3 integer constraint; direct arithmetic contradiction makes this structurally impossible

clifford.reason: A2 roots in Cl(2,0) = {+-e1, +-e2, +-(e1-e2)/sqrt(2) scaled}; B2 roots = {+-e1, +-e2, +-(e1+-e2)/sqrt(2)}; Clifford reflections from each system act differently on the same grade-1 vectors — cross-system interference
